```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
```

Repeated observations of a city or simulation often share the same spatial
support. `case` identifies each measurement instance. The native engine searches
each support row once, then applies its neighbors to all cases and variables.
Each case has its own population, regional proportions, income ranks, and
index normalizers.

## Two populations on one grid

```{r populations}
library(segcetera)
library(ggplot2)

city <- expand.grid(x = 0:9, y = 0:9)
city$year <- 2020L
city$A <- ifelse(city$x < 5, 9, 1)
city$B <- 10 - city$A
later <- transform(city, year = 2030L, A = ifelse(x < 5, 7, 3))
later$B <- 10 - later$A
observations <- rbind(city, later)

result <- seg_measure(
  observations,
  list(race = seg_categorical(c("A", "B"))),
  coords = c("x", "y"),
  case = "year",
  bands = c(0, 2, 4),
  output = "full"
)
result
as.data.frame(result)
```

The same `case` column appears in pairwise indices, exposures, local summaries,
retained scores/contributions, and diagnostic tables. Individual results remain
available in `result$cases`, with original ID values in `result$case_ids`.
Calls without `case` retain their ordinary result structure and tables.

```{r local-composition}
environments <- as.data.frame(result, what = "env")
environments$x <- result$coords[environments$location, 1]
environments$y <- result$coords[environments$location, 2]

ggplot(subset(environments, category == "A"), aes(x, y, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile() +
  facet_grid(case ~ band, labeller = label_both) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1), name = "A share") +
  coord_equal() +
  theme_minimal()
```

For `sf` input, `sf::st_as_sf(result, what = "env")` attaches the shared
geometries and retains the case column. Support row numbers have the same
meaning across all cases.

## Agreement with separate measurements

```{r compare}
separate <- lapply(split(observations, observations$year), function(d) {
  seg_measure(d, list(race = seg_categorical(c("A", "B"))),
              coords = c("x", "y"), bands = c(0, 2, 4), output = "full")
})
all(vapply(seq_along(separate), function(i) {
  isTRUE(all.equal(result$cases[[i]]$analyses, separate[[i]]$analyses))
}, logical(1)))
c(shared = result$diagnostics$focal_searches,
  separate = sum(vapply(separate, function(z) z$diagnostics$focal_searches, numeric(1))))
```

Radius weights are shared across cases. For kNN, cases with different eligible
populations may need different neighborhood radii. The shared search visits
enough candidates for every case; population selection, fractional boundary
shells, and adaptive weighting then use each case's own population.

```{r population-neighborhoods}
nearest <- seg_measure(
  observations, list(race = seg_categorical(c("A", "B"))),
  coords = c("x", "y"), case = "year", neighbors = "knn",
  bands = c(25, 100), output = "indices"
)
as.data.frame(nearest, what = "diagnostics")
```

## Support and bands

Cases are aligned by exact geometry, coordinates, or network node. Their row
order may differ. Use common, harmonized boundaries for polygon cases.
Repeated observations at a location contribute to one shared spatial site
within each case. Its full attribute distribution defines the focal composition.
An absent site has zero population; its local composition can still reflect
nearby populated sites. Such sites have zero population weight in overall
indices. Supplied rows with missing values follow the variable's `na.action`.

Omitted radius bands are calculated once from the common support with pooled
case populations as sampling weights. Explicit bands provide a fixed scale
when comparisons also involve independently prepared datasets.

Grid and pycnophylactic surfaces are prepared separately for each case on the
common source polygons. Their resulting supports are then aligned for shared
searches. Surface audit information is available per case in
`result$cases[[i]]$surface_info`. With `surface_audit = TRUE`,
`surface_info$locations` maps that case's prepared surface rows to the shared
support, and `surface_info$source_rows` maps common source polygon IDs to rows
in the original multi-case input. Absent source rows are `NA`.
